 Bracketeering is the game of strong opinions about stupid things, and one of the games in The Jackbox Party Pack 4 , where interstellar bracketeers place their bets to try and cheer their prompt to victory, or further another to double their cash.

 Contents

 1 Gameplay 

 2 Characters 

 3 Achievements 

 4 Promotional art 

 5 Trivia 

 Gameplay [ ] 

 For the first round, each player will be given a prompt (Example: "Best Grandma Name") and will answer it with an answer they see fit. Each answer will then be put into a bracket-style tournament where people vote for their favorite answers. AlI answers will be put in if either too few players are playing or there is an odd number of players.

 In round 2, the answers are put in mostly blindly, using a false prompt, but similar to the real one, for players to work off of. For example, the first prompt may be something like "Best Kitchen Tool," but may later change to "Best Thing to Kill a Goblin with" after each answer has been put in.

 In round 3, the prompt changes after every bracket ends.

 Before each round begins, players are put around a "prediction table" to bet on which answer will win each bracket. If the player guesses correctly, they earn some coins. The player who has the most coins by the end of the game, whether from the bracket itself or from the prediction table, is the winner.

 Trivia [ ] 

 The shark bracketeer is seemingly based off of the Predatory Loans mascot from Bidiots .

 Bracketeering has the second highest player capacity out of all of the Party Pack games, being able to have 16 players at once, only beaten out by Lie Swatter .

 A voice lines in the game reveal that the host's name is Dandelion .

 The fonts used are American Captain Eternal, American Captain Patrius, Revolution Gothic Bold, Revolution Gothic ExtraBold It, RevGothicOutline, RevGothicExtraBoldPhat, TRS Million Numbers & Impact.

 If you choose a prompt that was not written by a player, the winner will be credited to Arn .
 Arn is short for Arnie Niekamp, who is the person in the avatar. Arnie Niekamp is the editor for Bracketeering, so he curated all the wrong answers. Which is likely why the director decided to use him as the representation for the game's staff-made answers. [↑] 

 The only thing posted on Jackbox Games' official Soundcloud account is Bracketeering - It sure feels like a Wednesday! .

 Bracketeering is a party video game and one of five games featured in The Jackbox Party Pack 4 .

 Gameplay

 On the first round , a prompt is shown to every player in the game, of which they'll have to write an answer for it. Once all answers are in, a board of four answers, along with the player's own answer will show up, of which they'll have to pick the one that they think will win the match-up.

 When all predictions are in, four of the submitted answers are shown to everyone, which are separated into four other groups, and the players (along with the Audience ) will vote on which one they think is the best out of the bunch. If either time runs out or a vote isn't casted for a significant amount of time, the answer with the majority of the votes will win the match-up; however, in the case of a tie between the most voted answers, the players shall repeatedly tap on the answer that they chose, and the answer with the most taps overall will win the tiebreaker. The players will earn an amount of points depending on the percentage of the votes they've earned overall during that round, as well as a 500-point bonus if they managed to predict the winning answer correctly. This process repeats for the rest of the remaining match-ups. When all of the four match-ups have concluded, another prediction will be prompted, asking which of the winning answers will win the current 2v2 match-up, and the voting will work pretty much the same. After this, the list two winning answers will match-up with each other, with the winner of said match earning a 1,000 point bonus.

 The second round is the first "Blind Bracket" prompt, which will show a particularly vague prompt (like, name a vegetable, famous duo, etc.) that will relate to the actual prompt. The prediction and voting rounds will work just the same as the first.

 The third round also includes said Blind Bracket prompts used before, but with all of them changing with every match-up as opposed to it just being the same throughout the entire round. The points are also doubled this round.

 Once all rounds have concluded, all points are tallied up, and the player with the most at the end of the game will win.
